A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Perception-R1 work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, training analyses and manually assessed perception results.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds annotation audits, another training-data experiment and controlled reward-corruption tests.

M1.justification: The annotation-extraction pipeline, text-only judging LLM, visual perception reward, repetition penalty and GRPO optimization remain unchanged. Applying the pipeline to Mulberry with different data-curation models is an additional experimental application, not a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 extends training beyond Geometry3K through filtered Mulberry data drawn mainly from IconQA and DVQA, explicitly excluding geometry. It also uses GeoQA+ for comparative annotation analysis, without reporting model training on GeoQA+. The eight main evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V3 adds SophiaVL-R1-7B to both the main and vision-only comparisons. Table 1 also adds Qwen2-VL-7B-IT, previously evaluated in the appendix, and removes InternVL2.5-78B. Most comparator membership, including the component and approach ablations, is retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include a 100-sample correctness audit, annotation classification using 30-instance samples, 10% and 20% judgment-flip controls, and training on 16.8K Mulberry samples with different curation models. Figure 3a's averages now match all eight benchmarks rather than the four math benchmarks. Table 1 changes R1-VL's reported training count from 10K to 260K, although appendix Table 8 retains 10K; this does not establish retraining. Existing main splits, decoding and Perception-R1 hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands validation through annotation correctness and reasoning-contamination audits, training-data generalization, controlled reward-corruption tests, per-benchmark coefficient sensitivity results and computational-cost analysis. Appendix B.8 also adds MMMU and MMStar case studies. The earlier component, judge-size, Qwen2-transfer and reward-hacking analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 13 introduces approximate and 'with high probability' bounds for estimated baseline costs, providing limited qualitative uncertainty reporting without calibrated probabilities. The existing McNemar tests and one-sample t-test remain unchanged, and no new seeds, repeated-run counts or experimental confidence intervals are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 change Perception-R1's reported MMMU-Pro score from 41.4 to 42.4 under the same stated evaluation setting. Figure 3a replaces the gamma=0.7 average of 57.3 with 53.0, consistent with changed aggregation, while Figure 3b replaces WeMath results with MMMU results. V3 adds annotation, Mulberry, corruption, sensitivity and cost results, alongside additional baseline scores. Its Mulberry experiment reports a 2.1-point average advantage over GRPO trained on Mulberry. Vision-only model scores are retained, but adding SophiaVL reduces the reported MMMU-Pro comparison margin from 4.3 to 2.7.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, GRPO objective and reward definitions in Equations 1–5 remain mathematically equivalent. Renaming the objective from L to J is not a theoretical revision. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V3 narrows the introduction and conclusion from claims of new state-of-the-art performance to best performance against the compared baselines on most benchmarks. The central contributions concerning the perception bottleneck, visual perception reward and learning from 1,442 samples remain intact.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive interpretations concerning implicit reasoning distillation, Geometry3K's annotation composition, Mulberry's weaker mathematical coverage, sensitivity to corrupted judgments and computational tradeoffs. V2's dedicated limitations and future-work discussion is removed. Related noise and reward-hacking concerns remain in analyses, but the explicit qualification that these risks cannot be eliminated and the plan to reduce LLM reliance are not retained.

D1.justification: Existing training hyperparameters and prompts are largely relocated unchanged to Appendix C. New details include Mulberry curation-model identities, the division of GPUs between judging and policy training, and per-step and judgment timings. V2 says code and data are available; v3 uses future-release wording and adds a statement claiming supplementary code and data. Actual resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 adds SophiaVL-R1 and explicitly discusses methods that reward intermediate reasoning, while adding references supporting GeoQA+, IconQA, DVQA, Qwen3 models and other contextual discussion. The Ouyang et al. RLHF reference is removed. Most related-work organization and the positioning around neglected visual perception remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose are retained, with local language corrections and explanatory refinements. V3 reorganizes and expands appendix subsections, moves implementation settings into Appendix C, and adds reproducibility, acknowledgments and LLM-use statements. It also corrects Case Study 2's mismatched question to 'Find x.'

P2.justification: V3 adds five substantive tables and two illustrated case studies, and adopts conference formatting with revised title, headings, running headers and citation display. Figure 3 changes its average-performance axis and displayed benchmark selection; Figures 3c and 5 add smooth trend lines over training traces. Existing figures, prompts and tables are otherwise largely retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: The annotation audits, matched Mulberry-versus-GRPO comparison and controlled corruption tests strengthen evidence for assumptions and generalization that v2 left less directly tested. The gain is tempered by removal of explicit limitations and a new cost comparison that mixes measured timings with heuristic baseline estimates. The annotation composition analysis improves transparency but does not fully isolate perception gains from reasoning distillation.
